content.title: Why aren’t TSA workers getting paid? Answers for CSRA fliers
content.text: ATLANTA, Ga. — Airports across the nation, including Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, are facing long security lines due in part to the plight of Transportation Security Administration officers.These officers, who are employees under the Department of Homeland Security, have been working without pay since Valentine’s Day.Some of them have been quitting while others are increasingly calling out. In Atlanta, TSA callouts have reached nearly 40%.TSA workers are going without pay checks because Congress has failed to agree on full-year funding or a continuing resolution for DHS workers. This has led to a lapse in appropriations and has triggered a shutdown, which is a partial shutdown, of federal agencies.One thing a funding lapse does is stop paychecks.Because TSA workers are considered “excepted” federal employees, they are mandated to continue working even during a lapse in funding.“DHS employees furloughed or excepted during a lapse in appropriations do not receive payment for their regularly scheduled hours of work (furloughed employees) or actual hours worked (excepted employees) until after the lapse in appropriations ends,” the DHS website states.The good news? The workers will receive backpay once funding resumes.Federal immigration agents are seen at the Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, Monday, March 23, 2026, in Atlanta.(AP Photo/Emilie Megnien)TSA workers are paid through annual DHS funding, as well as aviation security/passenger fees that each passenger pays.According to TSA.gov, airlines charge travelers a passenger fee (or September 11 Security Fee) of $5.60 per one-way trip.The fee, which can’t exceed $11.20, is collected by airlines.At Atlanta’s airport, several travelers that Atlanta News First spoke to want TSA workers paid.“This is just kind of unfair to the busiest airport in the world,” Ferrari Simmons said. “We gotta do better. So if we can figure out a way to pay these people and get them what they need, we gotta do that. ASAP.”TSA lines are longer than ever at Hartsfield-Jackson International Atlanta Airport on Monday.TSA callout rates climbed over the weekend. Nationwide on Sunday, 11.8% of TSA agents missed work — the highest rate of the shutdown so far — with more than 3,450 officers calling out, according to DHS. More than 400 officers have quit during the shutdown, the department said.The Trump administration announced over the weekend that it would be deploying federal immigration officers at TSA checkpoints, and those agents were present at Atlanta’s airport Monday.Federal immigration agents are seen at the Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, Monday, March 23, 2026, in Atlanta. (AP Photo/Emilie Megnien)(Emilie Megnien | AP)Democrats are continuing to demand major changes to federal immigration operations — including policy changes that would require ICE officers to get a warrant from a judge before forcefully entering homes, the removal of masks and clear identifying information on uniforms.Critics have accused the government of using TSA workers as pawns in the ongoing budget fight. And some aviation unions have raised additional safety concerns in light of the Trump administration’s deployment of federal immigration officers.Copyright 2026 WRDW/WAGT. All rights reserved.
